messages:
maria: Customer reported 400 on embeddings endpoint. Error: "Invalid input shape: expected [n, dim] numeric arrays or list of strings, got nested arrays with inconsistent lengths (expected 1536 but found 1)". They say it used to work after a client change. Posting payload they sent below.

sam: can you paste the exact request body (redact keys)?

maria: yup forwarded. curl they used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-1-large","input":[[0.1,0.2,0.3]]}'
```
They were trying to send precomputed vectors but wrapped each vector twice (an extra array level) and sometimes sent a single scalar for one item.

henry: ahh yup that explains the dimension error. The service expects either: a) a list of strings (for text -> embedding) OR b) a list of numeric vectors where each vector is a flat list of length = model_dim (e.g., 1536). Common mistakes: sending a single vector without outer array, or double-wrapping causing shape like [[ [..] ]].

maria: customer originally used our SDK which handled shapes, then swapped to a homegrown batcher that concatenated streams and ended up flattening one item to a single number by mistake. Repro steps I ran locally: send a mixed payload with one item = 0 -> results in 400. Example showing wrong vs right:
```json
// wrong (nested/incorrect)
{"model":"embed-1-large","input":[[[0.1,0.2,...,0.3]], ["single text"]]}

// right (precomputed vectors)
{"model":"embed-1-large","input":[[0.1,0.2,...,0.3],[0.05,0.07,...,0.09]]}

// right (text inputs)
{"model":"embed-1-large","input":["first sentence","second sentence"]}
```

sam: actionable fix: validate client-side before send. Quick heuristics: if input contains any numbers, assert every item is a list and len == MODEL_DIM; if strings, assert all are strings. If mixed types -> reject. Also add guard against items that are ints/floats (scalar). We should add a snippet for them.

maria: pasted snippet to customer and suggested: wrap single vector in an outer array, or if you intended text embeddings convert text -> string array. They asked about throughput: they were trying to micro-batch by merging arrays themselves which caused the shape corruption. Any tips to recommend for safe batching?

sam: recommend using our SDK batch helpers or the server-side batch param (our API accepts up to 512 inputs per request depending on model). If they must batch client-side, do not mutate arrays in place; build a new list and validate shapes. Also enable our request tracing (x-rw-trace header) so we can link logs. For throughput, suggest sending fewer larger batches (but respect token and dimension limits) and enable async request pipeline rather than concatenating streams.

support-bot: Incident link created: https://console.redwood.ai/ops/trace/INC-1857777777, attached logs show 6 malformed requests in last 10m.

henry: i'll follow up with a small RFC to add a client-side validation example to quickstart docs and a snippet in SDK that raises clearer errors. For now marking root cause = client shape/encoding bug. Customer accepted fix and will patch their batcher. :thumbsup:

maria: closing once customer confirms deploy. Thanks all!
